Draft the citation and data availability text for an article

Source: R/data_availability_statement.R
data_availability_statement.Rd

data_availability_statement() drafts the text that the authors of an article need once the data package has a DOI: the reference list entry in APA style, the data availability statement and the in-text citation. All three come from metadata the package already holds, so they are ready the moment the DOI is on file.

The sources are:

PartSource
authorsAuthors@R in DESCRIPTION, roles aut and cre, in their order (the same persons as CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json)
yeardate-released in CITATION.cff, else Date in DESCRIPTION
title, version, licencePackage, Title, Version, License in DESCRIPTION
DOIdoi in CITATION.cff, which update_citation() writes
repositorythe GitHub repository in the URL field of DESCRIPTION
websitethe url in _pkgdown.yml, else the github.io entry of the URL field
download formatsthe CSV and Excel files in inst/extdata
withheld dataConfig/washr/withheld in DESCRIPTION

Usage

data_availability_statement(subject = "The data", clipboard = FALSE)

Arguments

subject

The opening words of the statement, which name the data the article uses. Defaults to "The data", which gives "The data supporting this study are openly available ...". Write it for the article, e.g., "The household survey data".

clipboard

Logical. Copy the reference entry and the statement to the clipboard as well? Defaults to FALSE. Needs the clipr package.

Value

A named character vector of class washr_data_availability with the elements reference, statement and in_text. Printing it shows the three parts.

Details

The reference entry follows APA 7: authors as "Family, I. I.", with "&" before the last one, and with 21 or more authors the first 19, an ellipsis and the last author. An author without a family name is an organisation and keeps its full name. The entry ends with the repository URL ("Available at ..."). The in-text citation names one author, two authors joined by "&", or the first author followed by "et al." for three or more.

The statement names the licence, the package and its version, the DOI and the in-text citation. When the package has a website, a second sentence points to it for the CSV and Excel downloads found in inst/extdata. When some data was left out of the package, write one sentence that says what and why into DESCRIPTION, for example Config/washr/withheld: Household coordinates are not included, to protect the privacy of the respondents. The sentence closes the statement word for word.

The function stops when CITATION.cff carries no DOI yet: run update_citation() with the DOI of the Zenodo record first. Run it on the released version; a development version (such as 1.0.0.9000) gives a warning, because the text would name a version that is not archived.

See also

Before: update_citation() with the DOI of the Zenodo record.

Other publishing functions: check_publication_readiness(), setup_readme(), setup_website(), update_website(), use_brand()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data_availability_statement()

# Name the data the article uses, and copy the text to the clipboard
data_availability_statement(subject = "The household survey data",
                            clipboard = TRUE)
} # }
